setup_note: Set GROCERY_PANTRY_DIR to a scratch directory before running these (e.g. a temp dir) so tests don't read/write a real installation's data. Run evals 1-3 in order against the same directory since each builds on the previous one's file state; evals 4-5 assume pre-seeded files as noted in their prompts.

evals.prompt: Add milk, eggs, and tissue to my grocery list
evals.expected_output: All three items appended to grocery-list.jsonl (under $GROCERY_PANTRY_DIR) as separate JSON lines, each with today's date as 'added'. No pantry changes. Brief confirmation, no over-explaining.
assertions: grocery-list.jsonl has one valid JSON line per item for milk, eggs, and a tissue/toilet-paper-type item
no line was added to pantry.jsonl
response does not ask an unnecessary clarifying question for a plain add

evals.prompt: (after eval 1) Just picked up the toilet paper and the eggs
evals.expected_output: Matches 'toilet paper' to the 'tissue' JSON line and 'eggs' to the 'eggs' line despite the wording mismatch; removes both lines from grocery-list.jsonl; appends both as new JSON lines to pantry.jsonl with today's date as 'bought'; gives eggs a reasonable 'expires' estimate and flags it as an estimate; tells the user these are now tracked in the pantry and to say so if not actually purchased.
assertions: the tissue JSON line is removed from grocery-list.jsonl despite the prompt saying 'toilet paper'
the eggs JSON line is removed from grocery-list.jsonl and a new eggs line is appended to pantry.jsonl
pantry.jsonl eggs line has a 'bought' field and either an 'expires' date or an explicit estimate flagged as such
response mentions pantry items can be removed if not actually bought
grocery-list.jsonl and pantry.jsonl remain valid JSONL (one parseable JSON object per line) after the edit

evals.prompt: (after eval 2) The bread I bought yesterday is in the freezer, not the counter
evals.expected_output: Finds the existing bread JSON line in pantry.jsonl and replaces it (whole line) with an updated 'notes'/'expires' reflecting freezer storage, not a duplicate new line.
assertions: pantry.jsonl has exactly one bread line after the turn (no duplicate)
the bread line's 'notes' or 'expires' field reflects freezer storage
the expires date, if present, was extended relative to counter storage
the edit was a full-line replace, not an appended second bread record

evals.prompt: What's going on with my kitchen stuff?
evals.expected_output: Proactively surfaces any pantry items expiring within 3 days or already expired (by parsing 'expires' fields in pantry.jsonl), without being asked specifically about expiry. Also mentions the current grocery list briefly.
assertions: response lists any pantry items expiring within 3 days or overdue, if present in pantry.jsonl
response does not fabricate expiry info for items with 'expires': 'unknown'

evals.prompt: (pantry.jsonl pre-seeded with a milk line whose 'bought' date is 24 days ago, no repurchase since)
evals.expected_output: Notices the stale milk record and asks whether the user is running low, offering to add it back to the grocery list, rather than silently ignoring it or silently re-adding it.
assertions: response proactively raises the milk staleness without being asked
response asks rather than assumes and auto-adds milk to grocery-list.jsonl
no low-stock nudge fabricated for non-staple/one-off items not in pantry.jsonl
